title: Agent Action Approve
summary: A review screen for an AI agent's tool call that spells out what it will delete, send or change and how far it reaches, before someone approves it.
description: Reads an agent's tool call and says plainly what it will delete, send or change, how far it reaches and whether it can be undone. Marks risky tokens, compares the agent's claim with the call, makes dangerous calls hold-to-approve and refuses risky "always allow" rules.
catches: Tokens that widen the reach: a lone \ (drive root), an unset $VAR, ../, 8.3 short names
A stated intent that disagrees with what the call actually does
MCP tools labelled read-only whose call writes or deletes
Commands hidden inside bash -c, cmd /c or encoded PowerShell, and curl | bash
"Always allow" rules that would also let through other commands, and refuses them for npx, bash -c, chained or irreversible calls
limits: A review UI only: whether a call is actually blocked depends on your host app honouring the decision
Static analysis of the call text; it cannot know what a script or binary does once run
Unknown tools and argument shapes are described less precisely than shell and SQL calls
"User approved this" does not mean the operation is safe
a11y: Decision result receives focus (tabIndex=-1) and status text is announced in a role="status" region
Hold-to-approve works with Space or Enter held down, not just the pointer
Refusals of an "always" rule use role="alert"
Risk level is shown with text and icon, not colour alone; motion respects prefers-reduced-motion
server: Enforce the decision at the tool boundary: the agent runtime must refuse calls that were not approved, and check the caller's authorisation for the target.
mistakes: agent ran rm -rf on wrong folder
